Base directory for this skill: /Users/owner/.claude/skills/video-use # video-use (bootstrap + operating mode + HyperFrames graphics + field notes) This skill installs the open-source editor https://github.com/browser-use/video-use and uses its own SKILL.md for the editing method, with two changes: it runs start to finish on judgment without asking questions (§0), and it builds graphics with HyperFrames (§3). Where this file and the upstream SKILL.md disagree, this file wins. ## 0. Operating mode: judgment, not questions Upstream is built around ask → confirm → execute. Here it runs straight through. - **No questions.** Don't call AskUserQuestion and don't end a turn on a question. Wherever upstream says ask, propose and wait, confirm, or let the user choose (process steps 3–4, Hard Rule 11, the palette, the music bed, the delivery format, "continue the last session?", "final render on confirmation"), decide with the defaults below and record the decision. - **Hard Rule 11 becomes "plan before cutting".** Write the strategy (4–8 sentences, as in upstream step 4) to `/project.md` before touching the cut, opening with an `Assumptions:` line for anything you had to guess. Then execute. Hard Rules 1–10 and 12 still hold. - **Read before deciding:** the user's message; `/project.md` (carry earlier sessions' canvas, fonts, palette and caption look forward unless told otherwise); any brief, notes, brand files or reference videos in the footage folder; and the footage itself (packed transcript plus `timeline_view` at decision points). - **Ambiguity → the most likely reading**, stated once in the hand-off. Vague feedback ("make it pop") → pick the most likely element, change one thing, say which. - **Stop only for a real blocker, and report it rather than ask:** no footage reachable, no transcription path when the edit depends on speech (§2), every source unreadable. First finish everything that doesn't depend on it (probe, inventory, contact sheet), then say in one or two lines what is missing and what it unblocks. - **Nothing irreversible:** sources are read-only, outputs go to `edit/`, and an earlier final is never overwritten (write `final_v2.mp4`). - **Deliver finished work.** After self-eval passes, plus the critic pass for anything that will be posted (reels, promos, ads), render the final, not just a preview. The hand-off is the file, its actual duration, aspect and loudness, the assumptions made, and anything left undone. ### Defaults when nothing says otherwise | Decision | Default | |---|---| | Canvas | Vertical source, or "reel / short / TikTok / story" → 1080×1920. Otherwise match the source aspect. Square or 4:5 only when asked. Changing aspect needs Mode B (§3.1). | | Length | Reels 20–45 s: keep the best, not everything. Long-form: tighten pauses and retakes, keep every point. Montage: the music's length, or ~30 s. | | fps | Match the source. | | Language | Detected from speech; captions in the spoken language. Hebrew → `--language he`. | | Captions | On for anything with speech headed to social; off for a wordless montage. 2–3 words a line, active-word highlight. Hebrew, Arabic or mixed lines → HyperFrames captions (§3.4). | | Hook | Open on the strongest line, with no title card in front of it. | | Grade | `none`, unless frames show a real problem (underexposure, colour cast, flat log) → a corrective grade only, checked on skin. | | Music | Only files the user supplied (footage folder or chat). Never download or generate music unasked; with no music file, ship without and say so. Several files → pick the one that fits the pacing and note the other. Duck under speech. | | SFX | Only when tied to a visible event; skip without a library. | | Graphics | §3.1, restraint first. | | Look | Brand files or `project.md` first. Otherwise one accent (sampled from the footage, or `#FFD60A`), white text with a soft shadow, Heebo 800 for Hebrew/mixed or Inter for English-only. Record it in `project.md` as the house style. | | Deliverables | `final.mp4` (H.264, yuv420p, AAC, −14 LUFS / −1 dBTP) plus `final.srt` when captions are burned in. | ## 1. Install (once per session) ```bash test -d ~/Developer/video-use || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/browser-use/video-use ~/Developer/video-use cd ~/Developer/video-use && (uv sync || pip install -e .) mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && ln -sfn ~/Developer/video-use ~/.claude/skills/video-use ~/Developer/video-use/.venv/bin/python ~/Developer/video-use/helpers/timeline_view.py --help >/dev/null && ffprobe -version | head -1 ``` Then **read `~/Developer/video-use/SKILL.md` in full** and follow it as amended by §0 and §3. Helpers live in `~/Developer/video-use/helpers/`. Run them with the repo's `.venv/bin/python`. Set up HyperFrames (§3.2) as soon as the plan includes a graphic. ## 2. ElevenLabs key + network - Transcription needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, from the environment or `~/Developer/video-use/.env`. If neither has it and the edit depends on speech, that is a §0 blocker: do the inventory, then say the key is needed (pasted in chat, or put in that `.env`). When the user pastes one, write it with `chmod 600`. Never echo the key, and never write it into the footage folder. An edit without speech (a music montage) goes ahead untranscribed. - The cloud workspace blocks `api.elevenlabs.io` unless the user adds it under claude.ai Settings → Capabilities → allowed domains. Test with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/models`. `000` means blocked: report it as a blocker and name the domain to allow. `401 missing_permissions` on /v1/user or /v1/models is fine for a scoped key: speech-to-text still works. - Hugging Face and the OpenAI model CDNs are blocked too, so there is no offline Whisper fallback (HyperFrames' own `transcribe` downloads its models from Hugging Face as well). Don't hunt for model mirrors. - Hebrew: pass `--language he`. Scribe diarization separates an off-camera producer (S0) from the speaker (S1), which is useful for dropping interruptions. ## 3. Graphics with HyperFrames HyperFrames (`heygen-com/hyperframes`) renders an HTML page with a paused GSAP timeline to video, frame by frame in headless Chrome. Upstream already lists it as one animation engine; here it is the default for graphics. Everything in §3 was checked end to end with CLI 0.8.180 (Oct 2026) in the cloud workspace: slot render, alpha composite through render.py's exact filter, Hebrew and mixed-language text, the caption layer. The CLI ships almost daily, so when a flag here disagrees with `npx hyperframes --help`, trust `--help`. ### 3.1 Judgment: what, which engine, which mode **What earns a graphic:** a hook title when the opening line doesn't hook on its own; a lower third the first time a person or product is named; a callout when the speaker says a number, a list or a step; an end card when there is a call to action. At most one new graphic element every ~3 s, the payoff landing on the spoken word (upstream's payoff-timing rule), the final frame held ≥ 1 s. No graphics at all when the footage carries itself. | Engine | Use for | |---|---| | **HyperFrames** (default) | Anything with text or layout: titles, lower thirds, callouts, counters and stats, lists, charts, end cards, follow/subscribe cards, progress bars, kinetic type, any Hebrew/RTL text, styled captions. Check the registry first (§3.3). | | Manim | Equations, formal diagrams, graph morphs (upstream vendors a Manim skill). | | PIL | A trivial static card, or when no Chrome can run at all. | | Remotion | Only if asked, or an existing Remotion brand system is in play. | **Mode A, overlay slots (default).** video-use owns the picture (cut, grade, HDR tone-map, scale, mix). Each graphic is a transparent HyperFrames clip that `render.py` composites. Right whenever graphics sit on top of the footage. **Mode B, HyperFrames finish.** video-use makes the cut decisions and HyperFrames composes the final. Choose it when graphics have to move or reframe the footage itself: changing aspect (render.py only scales, it never crops, so 16:9 footage stays 16:9), punch-ins, split-screen or picture-in-picture, B-roll moving with graphics, shader transitions. Also choose it when there are more than ~8 graphic elements. See §3.5. ### 3.2 Environment ```bash export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1 # init's --skip-skills flag is ignored; the env var works npx --yes hyperframes browser ensure || \ export HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH=$(ls -d /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-*/chrome-linux/headless_shell | tail -1) ``` - In the cloud workspace `browser ensure` fails (storage.googleapis.com is blocked), but a Playwright headless shell is preinstalled under `/opt/pw-browsers/`, which is the fallback above. Node 22 and ffmpeg are present. Re-export these variables in every Bash call and every sub-agent brief, because shell state doesn't persist. - `cdn.jsdelivr.net` is blocked, and the `init` scaffold and every registry block load GSAP from it, so their renders fail. Vendor GSAP and fonts once into `/animations/_shared/` and copy them into every slot: ```bash SH=/animations/_shared; mkdir -p $SH/vendor $SH/assets/fonts && cd $SH [ -f vendor/gsap.min.js ] || { npm pack gsap@3 --silent >/dev/null && tar -xzf gsap-*.tgz && cp package/dist/gsap.min.js vendor/ && rm -rf package gsap-*.tgz; } [ -f assets/fonts/heebo-hebrew-800-normal.woff2 ] || { npm pack @fontsource/heebo --silent >/dev/null && tar -xzf fontsource-heebo-*.tgz && cp package/files/heebo-{hebrew,latin}-{400,800}-normal.woff2 assets/fonts/ && rm -rf package fontsource-heebo-*.tgz; } ``` Then write `assets/fonts/heebo.css` with one `@font-face` per weight and subset, `url("heebo-hebrew-800-normal.woff2")` style paths (relative to the CSS file), `font-display: block`, Hebrew `unicode-range: U+0307-0308, U+0590-05FF, U+200C-2010, U+20AA, U+25CC, U+FB1D-FB4F`, Latin `unicode-range: U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6, U+02DA, U+02DC, U+2000-206F, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2212, U+FEFF, U+FFFD`. Other Fontsource families work the same way (`rubik`, `assistant`, `noto-sans-hebrew`, `frank-ruhl-libre`). Inter, Roboto, Montserrat, Poppins and Oswald are bundled and need no file. - A slot needs no `init`: a folder holding `index.html`, `vendor/` and `assets/` renders. - Speed here: about 6 s of wall time per second of 1080×1920 alpha output (2 cores, screenshot capture). A full-length caption layer for a 40 s reel takes 4–5 min. Parallel slot renders share the CPU. - On the user's Mac `browser ensure` and jsDelivr work, but vendoring still costs nothing and keeps renders offline and deterministic, so do it there too. ### 3.3 Mode A: one slot, end to end 1. **Canvas = the base render.py builds,** because it overlays at 0,0 without scaling. Portrait sources become 1920 tall and landscape sources 1920 wide, the other side following the source aspect (ffprobe the source, mind rotation tags). Build every slot full-frame at exactly that size, transparent everywhere except the graphic. `render.py --draft` builds a 1280 base, so overlays land wrong there: check overlays with `--preview`. 2. **Scaffold:** `mkdir -p /animations/slot_ && cd /animations/slot_ && cp -r ../_shared/vendor ../_shared/assets .`, then write `index.html` from the skeleton below. 3. **Registry first.** `npx hyperframes catalog --query "" --json` (447 items; works here), then `npx hyperframes add --no-clipboard`, which installs `compositions/.html` and prints a mount snippet. After adding: point GSAP at the vendored copy (`sed -i 's#https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@[^"]*/dist/gsap.min.js#vendor/gsap.min.js#' compositions/*.html`); replace placeholder text, avatars and colours; give the mount `data-start`, `data-duration` (≥ the block's own length) and a z-index, which the snippet lacks; rename the block's composition id in its file and mount if it is `main`; most blocks are 1920×1080, so prefer portrait ones for 9:16 or scale them in a wrapper. Useful for reels: `lt-clean-bar`, `lt-soft-pill`, `lt-dark-card`, `headline-slam`, `per-word-rise`, `titlecard-lockup`, `count-up`, `mk-progress-stat`, `chart-story`, `cta-lockup`, `cta-close`, `instagram-follow`, `tiktok-follow`. 4. **Check and render:** ```bash npx hyperframes lint # 0 errors npx hyperframes snapshot --at , -o snaps # transparency shows as white here: judge white text in the composite instead npx hyperframes render --format mov -o render.mov # ProRes 4444 with alpha ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=pix_fmt,width,height -show_entries format=duration -of compact render.mov ``` Gate: `pix_fmt` starts with `yuva` (it is `yuva444p12le`), the size equals the base, the duration equals the slot length. 5. **EDL entry:** `{"file": "/abs/path/to/edit/animations/slot_/render.mov", "start_in_output": T, "duration": D}`. Use absolute paths: render.py resolves overlay paths against the EDL's own folder, so upstream's `edit/animations/…` example becomes `edit/edit/…`. List order is stacking order (later is on top). `T` = the payoff word's output time minus the reveal time. 6. **Never `.webm` for render.py overlays.** Verified: ffmpeg's default VP9 decoder drops the alpha, and during the overlay window the whole frame turns black. MOV only. Skeleton (1080×1920; change the four size spots for another base): ```html
3 טעויות שכולם עושים
``` Rules that break slot renders (condensed from the edit-video skill's §0): - The root needs `data-composition-id`, `data-width`, `data-height` and `data-duration`. The render length is the root `data-duration`, never the GSAP length. - One paused timeline, registered after the last tween as `window.__timelines[""]`. A key that doesn't match the id makes the render wait ~45 s and then freeze. - Deterministic only: no `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance.now`, `requestAnimationFrame`, CSS `transition` or `repeat: -1`. Use a seeded PRNG for noise. - Tween transforms and opacity only. Use `fromTo` with an explicit start state and absolute values, and put `opacity: 1` in the destination of a reveal. Hide things in CSS, not with `tl.set(…, 0)`. Don't mix CSS `translate(-50%)` with GSAP `x` (use `xPercent`), and don't tween opacity on a `.clip` element itself. - Relative starts need spaces: `"intro + 0.5"`. - A sub-composition file wraps everything, styles and scripts too, in `
